digest.component_or_area: MCP error surface and CLI/library error code alignment
propositions: MCP tool failures currently arrive as unstructured prose in exception messages or divergent ad-hoc shapes, while the CLI already emits a structured error_envelope discriminator that agents need to distinguish failure types without pattern-matching English

The CLI's error codes (ticket_not_found, concurrency_conflict, claim_failed, etc.) are scattered across 12 call sites with no central vocabulary, forcing inconsistency between interfaces and making cross-interface testing impossible

The library interface exposes no machine error code uniformly — error_code_for(exc) must be created in _errors.py as a central classifier, re-exported as rebar.error_code_for, to give all three interfaces (library, CLI, MCP) a shared vocabulary source

MCP must catch rebar exceptions and raise McpEnvelopeError carrying a structured .envelope dict (via error_envelope) so agents receive a JSON discriminator on the raised ToolError.__cause__, not fragile prefix-stripped text

Two existing MCP soft-error returns (_mcp_reads explain_criterion and _mcp_llm) use divergent ad-hoc shapes and must be migrated to emit vocabulary error codes while preserving their existing agent-branching fields (kind, resolution_class, retryable, diagnostic)

The error_envelope schema must relax input from required to optional (keep error and message required) so target-less failures (gate refusals) are valid, while CLI envelopes remain unchanged; all three interfaces must agree on the code for identical failures via cross-interface test
